 LIVE UPDATES NBA Philadelphia 76ers vs. Detroit Pistons Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
 Andy Bailey Nov 4, 2026, updated just now 
 The Philadelphia 76ers (7-1) and Detroit Pistons (6-1) are in the midst of a potential Eastern Conference Finals preview on Wednesday, and we're here to bring you live updates, highlights and analysis throughout the contest.
 How is LeBron James so easily handling Detroit's physicality? Will Cade Cunningham find his jumper at some point in the night after a slow start?
 We'll answer those questions and a whole lot more as the game plays out.
 Live Updates
 14 Total Posts
 Newest First ​ Just Now 07:27 PM Getting Chippy in Detroit
 Joel Embiid used to champion the nickname "Troel" for himself, and it's not hard to see why when he plays.
 He's game is an almost constant source of instigation, from the way he tries to draw fouls, to how physically he defends to how much he puts the ball through the net. He has to be among the more frustrating matchups in NBA history.
 76ers 55, Pistons 42 - 0:36 left in the second quarter 
 15 mins ago 07:12 PM Not All Roses...
 ...But it's pretty darn close.
 Outside of this little blunder from Jaylen Brown, the Sixers have been cruising since about halfway through the first quarter.
 They're making just about every Pistons' attempt difficult and making good, quick decisions on the other end.
 76ers 48, Pistons 35 - 3:26 left in the second quarter 
 26 mins ago 07:01 PM Historic Night for LeBron James
 Given his 23-plus years of dominance, it feels like LeBron could break some kind of record or hit some kind of milestone in every game.
 We're not even halfway through the second quarter, and he already has two tonight.
 In addition to the record of 16,000 field goals noted by the Sixers, the ESPN broadcast shared that he assisted his 205th different player tonight. That's the most in the play-by-play era.
 76ers 43, Pistons 31 - 7:13 left in the second quarter 
 29 mins ago 06:58 PM LeBron Carving the Pistons Up
 LeBron James has only taken three shots, but he's completely dominating Detroit (the No. 1 defense in the league) anyway.
 He's up to five assists (with no turnovers) and making the right decision on seemingly every possession.
 76ers 43, Pistons 29 - 7:13 left in the second quarter 
 38 mins ago 06:49 PM Jaylen Brown Off to a Fast Start
 Philly's stars, with the possible exception of Maxey, are going to have to sacrifice plenty of scoring opportunities over the course of the season.
 Jaylen Brown already has, but he's been aggressive and effective tonight. Early in the second quarter, Brown has 12 points on 5-of-7 shooting.
 76ers 33, Pistons 25 - 9:52 left in the second quarter 
 42 mins ago 06:45 PM An Early Lead for Philly
 Duncan Robinson hit two threes in the first quarter, but the rest of Detroit's attack quickly ran out of juice after a decent start.
 Cade Cunningham missed too many jumpers, and the Sixers did a good job of rebounding and getting out on the break.
 Philly closed the quarter on an 18-4 run.
 76ers 29, Pistons 21 - 12:00 left in the second quarter 
 47 mins ago 06:40 PM B-Ball Paul!
 Paul Reed has pretty thoroughly outplayed his old teammate, Joel Embiid. He's bringing a lot more energy and looks more explosive, has four points (and another two called off by a questionable travel), while holding Embiid to 2-of-7 shooting.
 The Sixers, though, have locked in defensively. Detroit got off to a hot start on offense, but Philadelphia is challenging everything now. and they're getting out in transition after their stops.
 76ers 24, Pistons 20 - 0:44 left in the first quarter 
 1 hour ago 06:26 PM Back and Forth Early
 The leading scorers on these teams, Cade Cunningham and Tyrese Maxey, are really the only two who don't seem to be in a rhythm at the outset.
 76ers 11, Pistons 17 - 6:11 left in the first quarter 
 1 hour ago 06:22 PM Offenses Crisp Early
 Philadelphia and Detroit came into this game with the third and first-ranked defenses in the NBA, but it's their attacks that look sharp to start this one.
 Both teams are moving the ball, making the extra pass and getting out in transition.
 76ers 11, Pistons 14 - 6:50 left in the first quarter 
 1 hour ago 05:32 PM Stars Are Out in Detroit
 The Sixers have all their starters available for this one (which is notable for a team with a soon-to-be-42-year-old and Joel Embiid).
 2 hours ago 04:37 PM Eastern Conference Finals Preview?
 It's early, but it feels like the Pistons and 76ers are both good enough to represent the East in the Finals. And tonight could tell us a lot more about both teams.
 2 hours ago 04:30 PM Could Be In for a Big Cade Night
 The Sixers have a couple good options in Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe to hound Cade Cunningham tonight, but he's at home and has a chance to prove his team is still the class of the East.
 Over the last four seasons, Cade has averaged 24.3 points and 8.8 assists and is certainly capable of getting away from Brown and Edgecombe with some mismatch hunting.
 If he has a big night, the same will probably be true of the Pistons.
 3 hours ago 03:33 PM Tyrese Maxey Is Carrying the 76ers
 The 76ers had probably the splashiest offseason of any team in the league. And new additions LeBron James and Jaylen Brown are definitely helping.
 But Tyrese Maxey is undoubtedly the biggest reason Philadelphia is 7-1.
 He has around 86 percent of the team's total value over replacement player , is averaging 29.1 points and 5.3 assists and has been one of the league's more efficient volume scorers this season.
 Detroit has a lot of big, tenacious defenders to throw his way on the perimeter, but the best they can hope to do is slow Maxey down.
 6 hours ago 01:12 PM How Are the Pistons Proving Everyone Wrong?
 Detroit was widely regarded as a team due for a regression in 2026-27. But even without Jalen Duren for all but two games, the downturn simply hasn't come.
 The defense is the biggest reason why. The Pistons are giving up the fewest points per 100 possessions of any team in the league, and tenacious perimeter defenders like Ausar Thompson, Ron Holland and Cade Cunningham are a big reason why.
 Detroit's ability to stymie opposing offenses before they even break the three-point line has been huge. And Cunningham is engineering enough offense on the other end to give the Pistons one of the best point differentials in the league.
 The All-NBA creator is averaging 23.7 points and 7.1 assists. And for the first time in his career, he's on track for above-average scoring efficiency .
